sentences.text: Revenue compounded from $6.91 billion in FY2017 [F1] to $216 billion in FY2026 [F10], a 46.6% CAGR [F211].
Growth came in steps: 61.4% in FY2022 [D231], 0.2% in FY2023 [D284], then 125.9% in FY2024 [D338] and 114.2% in FY2025 [D393].
The FY2023 stall coincided with an 8.0pp gross margin drop to 56.9% [D298][F27], which the 10-K traces to $2.17 billion of inventory provisions [P35].
Operating margin reached 60.4% in FY2026 [F50], 27.6pp above the 32.8% window median [D813].
Data Center product revenue was $194 billion in FY2026 [S56], 89.7% of total revenue [D620].
Data Center contributed 60.2pp of the 65.5% revenue growth [D622][D448], so the largest driver supplies most of the increase.
The filing attributes Data Center growth to Blackwell demand, with computing up 59% and networking up 142% [P8][P10].
Operating expenses grew 40.7% against revenue growth of 65.5% [D468][D448], lifting incremental operating margin to 57.3% [D475].
Operating margin fell 2.0pp to 60.4% in FY2026 [D463][F50], still above the 32.8% window median [D813].
Gross margin fell 3.9pp to 71.1% [D462][F30] from 75.0% in FY2025 [F29], the largest cost-line effect in the FY2026 bridge [D477].
The filings cited do not explain that gross margin fall, but they quantify a $4.5 billion H20 excess-inventory charge in Compute & Networking [P7].
Operating expenses rose 40.7% on employee growth, compensation and compute infrastructure costs [D468][P9].
Other income of $11.1 billion [X120] partly offset the 15.1% effective tax rate [D434], leaving net margin at 55.6% [F70] against 60.4% operating [F50].
Operating cash flow was 0.86x net income [D435], $103 billion [F100] against $120 billion [F60].
Free cash flow of $96.7 billion [F110] was 0.81x net income [D436], the lowest level in the FY2022 to FY2026 window [D826].
In FY2023 operating cash flow fell 38.1% [D289], which the filing ties to the $1.35 billion Arm termination cost [P29].
Net cash was $2.14 billion in FY2026 [D441], against $34.7 billion in FY2025 [D386], or 1.0% of revenue [D442].

FY2026 short-term investments are absent from the filed lines [D439][X188], so FY2026 net cash, the 75.5% fall in cash and investments [D471] and the peer ranking [D844] are not comparable with earlier years.
Buybacks and dividends totalled $41.1 billion [D443], 42.5% of free cash flow [D444], and diluted shares fell 1.2% [D470].
Diluted EPS grew 66.7% [D452], slightly faster than net income at 64.7% [D450], so per-share growth tracked profit.
Customer concentration is the largest exposure: two direct customers were 22% and 14% of FY2026 revenue [P6], primarily in Compute & Networking.
Inventory rose 112.3% to $21.4 billion [D474][X222] against 65.5% revenue growth [D448], and days inventory reached 125 [D446].
Other income rose from $2.57 billion [X119] to $11.1 billion [X120], mainly from unrealized gains on equity holdings, including Intel [P3].
Net income therefore leans on non-cash mark-to-market gains, so operating income and cash flow are the better test of earnings quality.
Operating margin: a fall from 60.4% [F50] toward the 32.8% window median [D813] would reverse the step-up; check the FY2027 10-K.
Days inventory: above 125 days [D446] would confirm the build continues, while below 113 days [D391] would suggest it is unwinding; check the FY2027 10-K.
Gross margin: a reading below 71.1% [F30], moving toward the 56.9% window low [D817], would confirm that inventory charges are recurring; check the FY2027 10-K.
